processing_steps.atmosphere: 10^-5 mbar pressure, backfilled with argon gas atmosphere
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Remelted 5–6 times inside the arc melter (AM500-Edmund Buhler GmbH, Germany) without breaking the vacuum for better elemental intermixing.
Nine passes at 1050 °C in a 75-ton rolling mill, until the finish rolling temperature of 900 °C.
The air-cooled HR sheet was sectioned into smaller pieces for cold rolling.
CR sheets annealed at 900 °C for 5 min (sample denoted A5), followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic (γ) matrix containing elongated B2 stringer bands aligned along the prior rolling direction, unrecrystallized γ (URE-γ) pancake grains, and fine needle-like intragranular B2 (IG-B2) plus coarse intergranular B2 (GB-B2) after 900 °C/5 min annealing + water quench.

microstructure_list.region: overall annealed sheet (900 °C/5 min + water quench)

phases_present.morphology: matrix phase; includes coarse elongated unrecrystallized γ (URE-γ) pancake grains along prior RD and recrystallized γ (RE-γ) grains
three B2 morphologies retained after annealing: elongated lamellar B2 stringer bands along RD, fine needle-like intragranular IG-B2, and coarse blocky/irregular intergranular GB-B2

defects.type: bamboo-like B2 stringer grain structure (static recrystallization)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: URE-γ grains were coarse and elongated along prior RD by maintaining a pancake structure despite annealing; RE-γ grain size increases with annealing time.

precipitates.type: intragranular B2 (IG-B2), needle-shaped in unrecrystallized γ (URE-γ)
precipitates.distribution: nucleated at shear bands within URE-γ; net phase fraction 2.6%
precipitates.coherency: nonshearable BCC intermetallic in FCC γ; intragranular solid-state precipitation difficult through high coherency strain or activation energy barrier

precipitates.type: spherical-type intragranular B2 (IG-B2) in recrystallized γ (RE-γ)
precipitates.coherency: nonshearable BCC intermetallic in FCC γ; intragranular solid-state precipitation difficult through high coherency strain or activation energy barrier

precipitates.distribution: nucleating along prior austenite grain boundaries; coarse due to enhanced solute flux from grain boundary regions

phase_interfaces.coherence: BCC B2 in FCC γ; intragranular solid-state precipitation difficult through high coherency strain or activation energy barrier
grain boundaries inside statically recrystallized (bamboo-like) B2 stringer bands

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Macrovoids nucleate inside B2 stringer bands; crack initiation occurs at grain boundaries of B2 stringer bands; B2 stringer de-cohesion in segments leads to premature failure (A5 fracture surface annotated 'B2 stringer de-cohesion').

interfaces.slip_behavior: B2 is nonshearable; dislocations loop around B2 particles (Ashby-Orowan mechanism); strain concentrates preferentially in the softer γ.
interfaces.phase_evolution: δ-ferrite transformed into lamellar B2 stringer bands by hot rolling + cold rolling; annealing at 900 °C causes static recrystallization of B2 stringer bands plus IG-B2/GB-B2 precipitation.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge length 12.5 mm, gauge width 3 mm, thickness 2 mm; rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: 100 kN Instron 5982 with 10 mm gauge extensometer

elongation.uncertainty: rough reading from engineering stress-strain curve (Figure 5a)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of A5 (green) in Figure 5a: A5 is the highest-strength annealed condition but lower than HR/CR, extending to roughly 11% strain.

characterization_methods.technique: Field emission gun scanning electron microscopy (FESEM)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: etched in 3% nital; Figure 3a lower magnification 5 µm scale bar, Figure 3d/g higher magnification 1 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: observe annealed A5 microstructure (B2 stringer bands, URE-γ, IG-B2, GB-B2)
characterization_methods.key_findings: A5 shows elongated B2 stringer bands along RD, URE-γ pancake grains, fine needle-like IG-B2 and coarse blocky GB-B2 at grain boundaries.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: 100 kN Instron 5982 with 10 mm gauge extensometer
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; 1 mm min^-1 crosshead velocity; ASTM E8; RD; gauge 12.5×3×2 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: measure engineering stress-strain response and toughness of A5
characterization_methods.key_findings: A5 toughness 0.64 kJ/mol (90.1 J/cm³); A5 curve extends to roughly 11% strain and is the highest-strength annealed condition.

characterization_methods.purpose: fracture analysis of A5 tensile specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: A5 fracture surface shows 'B2 stringer de-cohesion' over elongated de-cohered stringers.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FESEM with routine EBSD setup; commercial software for raw data analysis
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electropolished in 10% perchloric acid + 90% acetic acid at 20 V, 5 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: EBSD phase map to identify crack initiation at B2 stringer band grain boundaries (Figure 5f)
characterization_methods.key_findings: crack initiation occurs at grain boundaries of statically recrystallized (bamboo-like) B2 stringer bands.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: outputs consistent with Ref. [15] for the same alloy composition

unmapped_findings: Standard-route A5 (900 °C/5 min + WQ, from the initial HR at 1 rpm + CR route) showed premature tensile failure driven by B2 stringer band de-cohesion; the improved properties quoted in the abstract (~1 GPa YS, 28% total elongation, 1.72 kJ/mol toughness) belong to the modified high-speed-HR route (Figure 6), not this standard-route A5 sample.
The IG-B2 is finer in A5 and tends to grow bigger into a needle shape through mutual coalescence in shear bands during annealing for 30 min (Figure 3d–f).
Total IG-B2 phase fraction = 3.7% (2.6% in URE-γ + 1.1% in RE-γ), consistent with the 3.7% IG-B2 mentioned in b0033.

γ-matrix phase fraction is reported as 64% in the modified-route strain-hardening discussion (b0033, b0046); it is not clearly attributable to standard-route A5 and was therefore not assigned to the A5 phase fraction fields.

TEM-EDX (Figure 4, on the longer-annealed A30) identified the B2 phase as Fe(Ni,Mn)Al with negligible carbon solubility; this B2 phase identity is alloy-level information relevant to A5's B2 stringer bands, IG-B2 and GB-B2.
